Something my parents did, as a kind of perfunctory thing, was to buy a preschool musical instrument package. No it didn't have a piano or a guitar, but it had a bunch of simple instruments for kids. They only did as part of a general external pose as creative educational parents(this was late 60s, my dad was a math professor), but they accidentally did me a huge amount of good.

I don't know if a kit like that is still available today, but if you can find one, you should make it available to your kids. Simple things like morracas and castinets, combined with the ready availability of a wide diversity of music will help them engage music enthusiastically on their own.

One of the best things to ever happen is that pianos are digital, and have shrunken down to the size of just the set of keys. My hope is to give my children the opportunity to learn piano on a real one, and practice at home on a cheaper one. If all goes to plan, I will buy a piano.
